results.result: The authors report a complete, densely reconstructed connectome of glomerulus VA1v using FIB-SEM at 8 nm isotropic resolution, identifying 192 neurons with >50 contacts that account for 87.9% of synaptic connections and 87% of glomerular volume, with 11,144 presynaptic T-bars and 37,843 postsynaptic dendrites at a density of 2.29 synapses/µm³.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C37, C59-C64, C69-C71 provide converging quantitative evidence for dense reconstruction completeness. The methodological details (8 nm isotropic FIB-SEM), neuron counts (192 with >50 contacts), coverage metrics (87.9% of connections, 87% of volume), and synapse counts (11,144 T-bars, 37,843 postsynaptic sites) are internally consistent and well-documented with specific figures referenced.

results.result: VA1v is characterized as a sexually dimorphic, fruitless-positive glomerulus that responds to sex pheromones (cis-vaccenyl acetate and methyl laurate), is larger in males than females, and contains 51 ipsilateral ORNs, 56 contralateral ORNs, 18 PNs, and 56 LNs.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C7 provide specific cell counts from the reconstruction, while C38-C40 cite established literature for VA1v's functional and anatomical properties. The characterization is well-supported by both current data and prior work, with appropriate citations (Sakurai et al. 2013, Kurtovic et al. 2007, Dweck et al. 2013, Kondoh et al. 2003, Stockinger et al. 2005).

results.result: The study reveals distinct synaptic polarity patterns: ORNs are predominantly presynaptic (with ipsilateral ORNs having more synapses than contralateral), PNs are predominantly postsynaptic, and LNs have approximately equal pre- and postsynaptic contacts with extensive reciprocity, except for LN2V which resembles PNs in connectivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C11 and C65-C68 consistently describe synaptic polarity patterns supported by quantitative data in the connectivity matrix (Figure 5, Figure 6). The characterization of LN2V as anomalous (C11, C87) is supported by specific connectivity data showing it receives ORN input and outputs to PNs, unlike other LNs.

results.result: The authors found 18 PNs in VA1v, significantly more than previously reported from genetic screens (Tanaka et al. 2012 reported ~1 PN/glomerulus on average; Tobin et al. 2017 reported 2-3 PNs in DM6), suggesting that GH146 Gal4 screens have not reached saturation and underestimate PN numbers.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C13 and C111-C120 present a coherent argument comparing current findings (18 PNs) with prior genetic screens. The comparison with multiple studies (Tanaka et al. 2012, Tobin et al. 2017, Grabe et al. 2016) showing lower PN counts supports the conclusion that genetic methods underestimate PN numbers. However, C115 notes that VA1v is among six glomeruli expected to have 6±2 PNs, so finding 18 is substantially higher even than this expectation.

results.result: The connectivity matrix reveals that ORN output dominates (59.8% of presynaptic connections), with 39.5% to PNs, 14.5% to LNs, and 5.9% to other ORNs; LN output accounts for 27.8% of synapses distributed evenly among targets; PN output within the glomerulus is rare (12.3% total); and ipsilateral ORNs provide 70% of total ORN input, with 76% of ipsilateral ORN-to-PN input going to monoglomerular PNs.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C15 and C72-C86 provide detailed quantitative breakdown of connectivity patterns with specific percentages that are internally consistent. The data are presented in Figures 5 and 7 with clear numerical values. The claim that most PN output lies outside the glomerulus (C81) is appropriately qualified as a prediction based on known anatomy.

results.result: Synapses in VA1v are characterized by T-bar ribbons opposite postsynaptic densities, with an average of 3.4 postsynaptic dendrites per synapse (range 1:1 to 1:9), forming predominantly triads and tetrads; synapse structure resembles other Drosophila neuropiles but with greater size variability; autapses occur in ~1% of PN synapses; and FIB-SEM preparation resulted in T-bars often lacking canonical profiles due to image contrast optimization.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C54 provide detailed structural characterization of synapses with specific quantitative data (3.4 average postsynaptic dendrites, range 1:1 to 1:9, ~1% autapses) and appropriate comparisons to other brain regions (lamina, medulla). The methodological explanation for T-bar appearance (C49-C50) is reasonable given the contrast optimization for membrane visualization. Figure 3 provides visual evidence.

results.result: Synaptic vesicles were not well resolved at 8 nm resolution; dense-core vesicles (50-100 nm diameter) were observed in most LNs; and a cell resembling 5-HT1 contained large dense-core vesicles (84±12 nm) with few synapses and projected via the mediolateral tract.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C58 acknowledge a limitation of the imaging method (C55) and describe vesicle observations with specific measurements. The identification of the 5-HT1-like cell (C57) is appropriately qualified as resembling the previously reported cell (Tanaka et al. 2012) with supporting quantitative data (84±12 nm vesicle diameter) and figure reference (Figure 3B-D).

results.result: Two LN types show anomalous connectivity patterns: LN2V resembles PNs more than other LNs, receiving input from ipsilateral ORNs and providing output mostly to PNs while being predominantly monoglomerular; and LN6 is almost entirely presynaptic with weak output to other LNs and strong output to LNv.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C89 describe specific anomalous LN types with distinctive connectivity patterns supported by the connectivity matrix data. LN2V's PN-like characteristics (C87) are well-documented in the results, and LN6's unusual presynaptic dominance (C89) is clearly stated. These findings represent novel observations about LN diversity.

results.result: Synaptic reciprocity analysis reveals that of 1540 neuron pairs with >2 contacts, 29% were reciprocal and 25% showed strong reciprocity (pre:post ratio ≥4 or ≤0.25); LN pairs constitute 85% of reciprocal pairs with average connection strength of 6.7±4.8 synapses; specific cell pairs show directed reciprocity (LN1-mPN1: 74% reciprocal with 2.2 ratio; LN2L-mPN1: 84% reciprocal with 1.5 ratio); mPN1s are highly reciprocal with each other (9.9 average strength); and ORN-to-mPN1 connections average 21.6±7.7 (ipsilateral) and 9.2±4.6 (contralateral) synapses.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C99 provide comprehensive quantitative analysis of reciprocal connectivity with specific percentages, ratios, and synapse counts. The data are internally consistent and presented in Figure 8. The comparison with Tobin et al. 2017 (C99: 23 synapses from ipsilateral ORNs) shows good agreement with current findings (C97: 21.6±7.7).

results.result: The study provides the first complete connectome of a sensory glomerulus in Drosophila, complementing previous EM studies (Rybak et al. 2016, Tobin et al. 2017) by comprehensively documenting LN circuits that constitute nearly half the glomerular cells; FIB-SEM's superior z-axis resolution aided reconstruction of dense LN arbors; dense reconstruction ensures all cells are detected; and agreement between FIB-EM and Gal4 labels validates both methods, though most LNs are multiglomerular and incompletely reconstructed beyond VA1v.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C110 appropriately position the study's contributions and limitations. The claim of providing comprehensive LN circuits (C100-C101) is supported by the data showing 56 LNs reconstructed. The methodological advantages of FIB-SEM (C102) and validation through agreement with genetic labels (C108) are reasonable. The acknowledgment of limitations (C107, C110) regarding multiglomerular LNs is appropriate and honest.

results.result: The synapse density in VA1v (2.29 synapses/µm³) corresponds approximately to values reported by Rybak et al. (2016) for glomerulus VA7 but is less than the density in the optic lamina and medulla.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 make appropriate comparisons with prior work (Rybak et al. 2016) and other brain regions (Meinertzhagen 2014). The comparison is appropriately qualified as 'approximately' corresponding given different computational methods, and the lower density compared to visual neuropiles is a reasonable observation.

results.result: VA1v is innervated by sensilla containing olfactory receptors involved in courtship and mating; the large number of PNs (18) is predicted to improve detection accuracy and latency of odor stimuli and may encode diverse stimulus features.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C118 appropriately cite prior work for VA1v function (Grabe et al. 2016) and make reasonable predictions about the functional significance of having many PNs (Jeanne and Wilson 2015, Grabe et al. 2016). The predictions (C117-C118) are appropriately qualified and based on cited theoretical work.

results.result: The study was unable to reliably identify putative gap junctions between neurons due to the tortuosity of tightly woven neurites preventing visualization of linear membrane stretches with appropriate densities.
results.evaluation: Claim C121 honestly acknowledges a limitation shared with other connectome studies (Rybak et al. 2016, Tobin et al. 2017, Takemura et al. 2013, 2015) and provides a reasonable explanation for why gap junctions could not be identified in this preparation.

results.result: ORNs and PNs (projecting to mushroom body calyx and lateral horn) express a cholinergic phenotype, while LNs are likely either GABAergic (inhibitory) or glutamatergic (probably also inhibitory).
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C125 appropriately cite prior work for neurotransmitter phenotypes (Wilson 2013, Yasuyama et al. 2002, 2003, Wilson and Laurent 2005, Okada et al. 2009, Seki et al. 2010, Liu and Wilson 2013). The characterization is appropriately qualified as 'likely' for LNs given the cited evidence.

results.result: Synaptic reciprocity is widespread in many brains and was first demonstrated in early EM studies of vertebrate olfactory bulb and retina; the ratio of strongly reciprocal pairs in VA1v (0.25) is comparable to other systems (Ciona tadpole: 0.39).
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C130 provide appropriate historical context (Rall et al. 1966, Dowling and Boycott 1966) and comparative data (Ryan et al. 2016). The comparison of reciprocity ratios across species is reasonable and well-cited.

results.result: Silencing LN1 and LN2 cells in the entire antennal lobe fails to modulate glomerular input or output activity, suggesting they may play a role in more local interactions on a global or longer time scale rather than in odor identity coding.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C132 cite functional evidence (Strube-Bloss et al. 2017) and make a reasonable inference about LN function based on the silencing experiments. The prediction (C132) is appropriately qualified as 'possible' and 'suggesting.'

results.result: The specimen was a 6-day female Drosophila (w1118 × CS cross) prepared by high-pressure freezing and freeze substitution; ~8,900 FIB-SEM images were acquired at 8 nm/pixel resolution with 2 nm milling steps, summed in sets of four to generate 8×8×8 nm isotropic voxels; automated synapse detection generated >500,000 synaptic puncta for the entire antennal lobe; two trained proofreaders with >85% recall and >94.7% precision annotated synapses; the analysis required 60 person-months of proofreading and 20 person-months of curation.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C144 provide comprehensive methodological details with specific parameters, quality metrics, and effort quantification. The methods are well-documented with appropriate citations (Takemura et al. 2013, Knott et al. 2008, Xu et al. 2017, Huang and Plaza 2014, Kreshuk et al. 2011, Zhao et al. 2015). The quality control procedures (C141-C143) demonstrate rigor.

results.result: The introduction provides context on olfactory system organization in insects and mammals, Drosophila ORN and PN organization, LN classification, and previous EM studies of antennal lobe glomeruli, identifying gaps in comprehensive LN circuit documentation.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C36 provide appropriate background context with extensive citations to prior work. The characterization of previous studies (C34-C36) and identification of gaps in LN circuit knowledge appropriately motivates the current study. All claims are well-supported by cited literature.
